title: Addy Osmani's LLM Coding Workflow for 2026
description: Addy Osmani shared his comprehensive LLM coding workflow going into 2026, detailing how he plans, codes, and collaborates with AI. The article distills tips and best practices from his experience, providing practical guidance for developers looking to effectively integrate AI coding tools into their workflow. This reflects the maturation of AI-assisted development practices as developers establish more sophisticated patterns for human-AI collaboration.
author: Addy Osmani

title: Loop Engineering: Designing When AI Must Stop
description: A new engineering discipline emerged in July 2026 called 'Loop Engineering' — focused on 'designing when AI must stop' and managing hidden work around coding agents. This represents a maturation of AI engineering practices, moving beyond simply enabling AI agents to thoughtfully constraining their behavior. The discipline addresses the challenge of managing autonomous coding systems while maintaining oversight and preventing unintended consequences.
author: Industry Observers

title: Best LLMs for Coding in July 2026
description: Multiple sources released rankings of the best AI coding models for July 2026. Top performers include Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, GLM-5.2, and DeepSeek V4-Pro. For open-source, GLM-4.7 is highlighted as scoring 94.2% on HumanEval and 73.8% on SWE-bench, competitive with Claude Sonnet. The rankings reflect rapid advancement in LLM coding capabilities and increased competition among model providers.
author: Various AI Researchers

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.6: Sol, Terra, and Luna Models
description: OpenAI released the GPT-5.6 model family in three sizes on July 9, 2026: Sol (flagship), Terra (balanced/agents), and Luna (efficient). GPT-5.6 Sol achieved state-of-the-art results with 92.2% on BrowseComp and 62.6% on OSWorld 2.0, surpassing Opus 4.8 while using 85% less compute. The launch had been delayed due to U.S. government concerns. Pricing: Sol ($5/$30 per 1M tokens), Terra ($2.50/$15), Luna ($1/??). This marks a significant milestone in frontier model capabilities for coding and reasoning tasks.
author: OpenAI

title: Meta Launches Muse Spark 1.1 with API Access
description: Meta released Muse Spark 1.1, the first Spark model to offer an API. Meta claims significant improvements in agentic tool calling and computer use. Simon Willison created llm-meta-ai, a new plugin for LLM providing CLI and Python library access to the model. The evaluation report includes interesting 'Attractor States in Self-Conversation' experiments where two copies of the model talk to each other.
author: Meta (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Rewriting Bun in Rust using Agentic Engineering
description: Jarred Sumner published a detailed account of rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust using modern coding agents, showcasing sophisticated agentic engineering with dynamic workflows, trial runs, and adversarial review. The rewrite took 11 days and cost $165,000 in API tokens (5.9B input, 690M output, 72B cached). The key insight: 'Until very recently, programming language choice was a one-way decision' — but today's frontier models change that equation entirely. A crucial enabler was the TypeScript test suite acting as a conformance suite, allowing an agent harness to automate much of the port.
author: Jarred Sumner (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Kenton Varda's Moratorium on AI-Written Change Descriptions
description: Kenton Varda declared a moratorium against AI-written change descriptions (PR/commit messages, issues/tickets) from his team, stating that 'AI was writing change descriptions that were worse than useless to me as I tried to review PRs: outlining details of the code that could easily be seen by looking at the code, but omitting the higher-level framing needed to understand broadly what the code is doing.' This highlights a critical gap in AI-assisted development: tools can describe mechanics but struggle with strategic context.
author: Kenton Varda (covered by Simon Willison)

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-Live Voice Mode
description: OpenAI finally upgraded the model used by ChatGPT voice mode with GPT-Live. The new model can spin off harder tasks to GPT-5.5 in the background while maintaining conversation flow. For questions requiring web search, deeper reasoning, or complex work, it delegates to the latest frontier model and brings results back into the conversation. The previous voice mode was based on a GPT-4o era model with a knowledge cutoff in 2024.
author: OpenAI (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Tencent Releases Hy3 MoE Model
description: Tencent released Hy3, a 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 21B active parameters. Following the Hy3 Preview launch in late April, Tencent gathered feedback from 50+ products and scaled up post-training with higher quality data. Hy3 outperforms similar-size models and rivals flagship open-source models with 2-5x parameters. The full-sized model is 598GB on Hugging Face, with a 256K context length. Available for free on OpenRouter until July 21st.
author: Tencent Hy Team (covered by Simon Willison)

title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2: Mostly Written by Claude Fable for $149.25
description: Simon Willison used Claude Fable 5 to help get sqlite-utils 4.0 to a stable release, with Fable writing most of the code. The cost was approximately $149.25 for the work. The experience shows how modern coding agents can handle substantial development work on existing codebases while maintaining quality standards. Simon emphasizes that he tries to keep to SemVer and make incompatible major versions as rare as possible.
author: Simon Willison
